messages.author: e638db67acbf6128
messages.subject: Plotting hours, minutes, seconds
parts:
Before I give an extended example, I will just ask this: is ggplot2
supposed to support sub-date precision for axis labels, etc? I am
seeing several strange errors when I try to plot vectors of the class
POSIXct (good old plot() has no trouble with the same data).

> dx <- data.frame(time = as.POSIXct(seq(100000, 200000, 1000), origin="1970-01-01"), value = rnorm(101))
> qplot(time, value, data=dx)
Error in if (prec$unit == "sec") { :
missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed

-Dan

>
> Yes, it is supposed to work.

Were there any bugs in POSIXct handling that have been fixed in the
development version? I ask this because I earlier had a problem where
ggplot2 would freeze (or perhaps eat all my memory – I don't recall) on
a dataset (of moderate/large size) when plotting POSIXct variables and
adding major="months", major="days" or something similar.

The variables were actually dates, so converting them using as.Date
solved the problem.

Unfortunately, I don't have the dataset any longer. But I did use the
latest official version of ggplot2.

--
Karl Ove Hufthammer

I still have a problem with scale_x_date(). I am using R version 2.9.2 (2009-08-24), ggplot2 version 0.8.3. Here is an example that shows the problem.

> t <- c( 1256021854, 1256022095, 1256022376, 1256022665, 1256022892, 1256023141)
> foo <- data.frame(time = as.POSIXct(t, origin="1970-01-01"), value=1:6)
> p <- ggplot(data=foo, aes(x=time, y=value))
> p + geom_point()
> p + geom_point() + scale_x_date()
Error in fromchar(x) :

-Dan
